title: Coupang celebrates America’s Small Business Saturday with global reach
summary: Discover how Coupang helps U.S. small businesses overcome export hurdles, reach international customers, and reinvest global revenue into local growth.
body_markdown:
Small businesses are the backbone of the American economy. Across the country, these entrepreneurs drive innovation, create local jobs and anchor their communities. Small Business Saturday, which is recognized by the U.S. Congress, the U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) and governments in all 50 U.S. states, celebrates the grit and ingenuity of American entrepreneurs.[Coupang](https://www.aboutcoupang.com/how-coupang-american-tech-company-went-global/) is proud to connect these local brands with international consumers, fueling economic growth right here at home.


“Small businesses across the country are continuing a great American tradition of innovating to reach new customers and create lasting value,” said Coupang Chief Global Affairs Office Robert Porter. “By partnering with Coupang, American entrepreneurs can succeed in international markets and turn global commerce into economic growth in their local communities.”


Coupang drove more than $5 billion in sales and exports of American goods overseas in 2025, reaching millions of customers by working with thousands of U.S. businesses.


## **** **Taking American innovation global**


For many small business owners, expanding overseas feels out of reach due to complex logistics and regulatory hurdles. Coupang reduces those barriers by handling the heavy lifting of cross-border commerce on their behalf, allowing small business owners to focus on what they do best: making high-quality American products.


For example, in Malden, West Virginia, Nancy Bruns revived her family’s multi-generation salt business,[J.Q. Dickinson Salt-Works](https://www.aboutcoupang.com/wv-based-business-reaches-millions-of-new-customers-overseas-with-coupang/) , but as the business flourished, she hoped to grow beyond the U.S. market. After spending more than a year researching the complexities of international labeling and freight, she found a solution.


“Coupang definitely took the intimidation out of international selling,” Bruns says. “Moving the product from U.S. soil into foreign markets is a huge lift for a small business like ours, and for Coupang to take that on is incredible.”


J.Q. Dickinson Salt-Works CEO Nancy Bruns and U.S. Representative Carol Miller (R-WV) inspect salt samples.


**** Jeff Golini started All-American Pharmaceutical, the parent company of **[EFX Sports](https://www.aboutcoupang.com/efx-sports-coupang-global-growth/) ,** with a $3,500 investment, selling amino acid tablets out of his gym bag. Today, exports play an important part of the Billings-based company’s business, feeding directly back into the local tax base and workforce.


“Having a partner like Coupang that handles our exports really saves a lot of time on my end and our staff’s end,” Golini explains. “That’s one of the reasons why we have grown so fast with them — we can concentrate on product development versus spending all of our time figuring out how to get our products into a different country.”


All-American Pharmaceuticals CEO Dr. Jeff Golini and U.S. Senator Tim Sheehy (R-MT) discuss export opportunities for Montana businesses.


Coupang’s support for small businesses goes beyond helping them export — the company is also investing in technologies that the company believes will accelerate the pace of U.S. exports in the future.


In Austin, Texas,[Contoro](https://www.aboutcoupang.com/coupang-ai-investments-contoro-robotics/) founder Youngmok “Mok” Yun is taking his American-developed AI logistics technology to international markets. Contoro is engineering and building AI-driven robotic arms that collaborate with human workers to unload shipping containers, increasing efficiency and safety. Supported by Coupang’s global infrastructure and startup mentorship, Contoro is working to launch a pilot for the technology in Korea and beyond.


“One thing I really love about Coupang is that it was a technology startup in the U.S.,” Mok shares. “They understand our problems, they want to share their experience with Contoro and they want to help us grow fast.”


Contoro’s AI-enabled robotic arms are designed to collaborate with human workers to unload shipping containers.


**** When American small businesses win overseas, those sales create reliable revenue streams that owners reinvest into new equipment, local hiring and community partnerships. This Small Business Saturday, supporting local entrepreneurs means championing businesses with roots in American communities and reach across the globe. By turning international commerce into local jobs and growth, Coupang is proud to help American small businesses thrive at home and abroad.


## Frequently asked questions


How does Coupang help U.S. small businesses sell internationally?


Coupang reduces the barriers to cross-border commerce by handling complex international logistics, freight and regulatory hurdles on behalf of small business owners. This allows American entrepreneurs to focus on product development rather than the many challenges of exporting.


Which U.S. small businesses are featured in Coupang’s Small Business Saturday spotlight?


The post highlights three American businesses expanding globally with Coupang: J.Q. Dickinson Salt-Works in Malden, West Virginia, is a seventh-generation family salt business revived by Nancy Bruns. All-American Pharmaceutical/EFX Sports in Billings, Montana is a sports nutrition company founded by Dr. Jeff Golini. Contoro Robotics in Austin, Texas is an AI logistics robotics startup led by Youngmok “Mok” Yun. Each of these businesses, and thousands of other U.S. companies, are working with Coupang to expand opportunities in overseas markets.


How do international exports benefit local U.S. communities?


Reaching overseas consumers creates reliable revenue streams that small business owners reinvest directly back into their local economies. These funds support local hiring, investments in new equipment, research and development, community partnerships and the local tax base.
